sq.t: Iron Age to medieval sites south of church
sq.x: GGAT recorded an Iron Age farmstead, Roman occupation, a medieval monastic grange, a late medieval site and farm, and a Norman earthwork castle south of St Dochdwy’s church.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

sq.t: St Dochdwy's: possible early monastery, c.650
sq.x: St Dochdwy's church beside the farm is thought to have been an early monastery around 650 (source pending).

sq.t: St Dochdwy’s churchyard may date to 7th century
sq.x: GGAT recorded that the church of St Dochdwy and its surroundings are of considerable archaeological interest, the churchyard likely on the site of an earlier foundation perhaps dating to the seventh century AD (Davies 1978).
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

sq.t: Llandough confirmed to Tewkesbury Abbey, c.1106
sq.x: About 1106 the Llandough settlement was confirmed to Tewkesbury Abbey; a grange was later established at Llandough (1994 excavation report).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: Medieval timber building beside St Dochdwy's
sq.x: Heneb record GGAT03583s records postholes of a possible medieval timber building immediately north of St Dochdwy's, in the Great House Farm excavation area, with 12th–14th-century pottery; the excavators describe a rectangular building of possible 13th- or 14th-century date.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: 1392: Cwm-Cedwyn in Llandough boundary records
sq.x: A medieval reference of 1392 to Cwm-Cedwyn is recorded in Llandough boundary records. (source pending)

sq.x: Llandough boundary records of 1392 refer to Cwm-Cedwyn (EV-0001; primary document not yet held).

sq.t: Manor of Llandough East held by Tewkesbury, 1535
sq.x: In 1535 the manor of Llandough East belonged to the Abbot of Tewkesbury and had free and villein tenants paying rents of assize (Cardiff Records).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: Llandough manor passes to the Herberts, 1543–45
sq.x: Henry VIII granted Llandough manor in 1543 to Lord Clynton and Say and Robert Turwitt; by 1545 Sir George Herbert held it, as a rent-roll shows, and he appears to have conveyed it to his grandson Sir William Herbert (Cardiff Records).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: 1547: Herbert’s 1,000-year Cydwin lease to Vaughan
sq.x: A 1547 lease of Cydwin for 1,000 years by Sir George Herbert to Vaughan is recorded as an evidence lead; the exact land is not yet identified. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E173 — Cedwyn / Cwm-Cedwyn: complete reference index

sq.t: Herbert grants Vaughan 1,000-year lease of Cydwin
sq.x: In 1547 Sir George Herbert granted Vaughan a 1,000-year lease of Cydwin (EV-0002; primary document not yet held).

sq.x: Bute Estate records from 1552 to 1824 name the farm Cedfin, Cydfin, Ken fin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm (GHF-E179); the identity of each entry with the farm is a research lead.

sq.x: The National Library of Wales holds D219 leases of “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm”, a 107-acre holding, 1552–1824. NLW noted Ty Mawr translates as Large House or Great House; the identity with this farm is not yet shown.

sq.t: Llandough with free tenants and copyholds, 1596
sq.x: In 1596 Landoche-juxta-Cardif was recorded as having free tenants, demesnes and copyholds (Cardiff Records).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: Farmhouse largely 17th-century with earlier fabric
sq.x: The 1994 excavation report records that the farmhouse, largely 17th-century but possibly incorporating earlier fabric, and its outbuildings stood on the site until demolition in 1988; it associates 19th-century work on the house with the Bute Estate.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: Farmhouse may have held 17th-century fabric
sq.x: GGAT recorded the farmhouse as of considerable archaeological interest; though structural and documentary evidence was incomplete, it may have contained parts of a seventeenth-century building. The report notes an ownership dispute and the 1988 demolition.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

sq.t: Farm dated 1667, about 45 acres
sq.x: Mary's statement records the date 1667 for the farm and a holding of about 45 acres reaching across Leckwith Road, of which about 10 acres around the farmhouse remained by c.1974.

sq.t: Occupation of the house dated to 1667
sq.x: The record dates Williams occupation of the house to 1667 and shows the Williams as tenants of the Bute Estate by the nineteenth century.
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

sq.t: Williams connection to the house since 1667
sq.x: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr) stood beside St Dochdwy’s Church, Llandough-juxta-Penarth. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 statement traces the family’s connection to the home to at least 1667.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm: Case Overview and Key Records

sq.t: Llandough manor to Bute line, 1767–1793
sq.x: In 1767 the manors of Dinas Powis, Landough East and Cogan were held by William Hurst and Calvert Richard Jones; Llandough followed Cogan, bought by the Earl of Bute in 1793. This does not show Great House Farm passed in the same instrument.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: 1824 Bute survey: Cedfin or Ty Mawr tenanted
sq.x: David Stewart’s 1824 survey of the Bute Glamorgan estates (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1) recorded plan 19, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, Llandough: 139a 3r 8p including about 20 acres of wood, let to “John Gedrick Tent.”, with land of the “Late Thos. Williams” added. The tenant’s name reading needs the archive image.

sq.t: c.1841 tithe: Williams occupier of Bute parcels
sq.x: The c.1841 tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists John Williams as occupier of 36 parcels, about 119½ acres: 33 owned by “Bute the Marquess of” and 3 glebe parcels of the Revd James Evans. No lease, term or rent is recorded.

sq.t: Museum places armour finds at Church Farm
sq.x: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales replied: “It is stated that these objects were found at Church Farm, Llandough, in 1858,” resting on a letter headed Cogan Pill, 22 November 1931 (FOI 2026-036). The Museum holds nothing of a similar nature from Great House.

sq.t: Llandough Farm was a separate Rees holding
sq.x: The Rees family held a farm called Llandough Farm, rented from the Bute estate, from at least 1865 to 1910. It is named separately from John Williams’s Great House farm, so records naming “Llandough Farm” do not by themselves refer to Great House.

sq.t: 1870s rate books: Williams occupier, Bute owner
sq.x: Llandough poor-rate books of 1872–1876 list “John Williams | Lord Bute | Farm”: John Williams rated as occupier of a farm (about 76 acres) owned by Lord Bute, with Lord Bute rated for woods in his own occupation.

sq.t: 1876 rate book: farm owned by Bute
sq.x: The 1876 rate book (provisional reading, EV-0212) shows the farm, about 76 acres, owned by Bute, and 32 acres of woods in Bute’s own hands.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

sq.t: 1876 poor rate: farm owned by Lord Bute
sq.x: The Llandough poor rate of October 1876 records John Williams rated for a farm of about 76 acres, owner Lord Bute; Lord Bute for woods in hand, 32a 3r 39p; Daniel Thomas & Son for a lime kiln and quarry (provisional; EV-0212).

sq.t: Manorial courts held at Great House
sq.x: In the early nineteenth century the Bute Estate acquired the freehold of Great House, previously the Vaughan family’s chief freehold farm; the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith were held in the house (HER GGAT02038s). How Bute acquired it is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)

sq.t: Bute deeds: dwelling by churchyard, 1811
sq.x: The NLW Bute title-deeds list describes D153/1–8 as deeds for premises in Llandough parish, 1811–1912, including a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard in 1811 (D153/1–2).

sq.t: 1824 survey: “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”
sq.x: Stewart's 1824 survey of the Bute estates, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”: 139a 3r 8p including 20a 2r 35p of wood; tenant read as John Gedrick; 10a 3r 39p of “late Thos. Williams” land added (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1; EV-0211).

sq.t: 1824 survey: “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”
sq.x: The 1824 survey plan DB/E/1 plan 19 lists “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” at 139a 3r 8p including woodland (transcription provisional).

sq.x: An image titled “1824 map of Ty Mawr” is held. It shows Tŷ Mawr as a named holding in the early nineteenth century; its creator, series and scale are still to be confirmed from the original (source pending).

sq.t: Map of Tŷ Mawr dated 1824
sq.x: A map of Ty Mawr dated 1824 is held (EV-0004); whether 1824 is the map date or an associated reference is not yet established.

sq.t: Historical map labelled “1841-map”
sq.x: A historical map labelled “1841-map”, likely linked to the tithe survey, is held. It can help reconstruct the field names and the boundaries of the Great House Farm parcels; its exact title and archive reference are still to be confirmed (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E165 — Historical map labelled “1841-map” (original image upload)

sq.t: Historical map labelled “1841-map”
sq.x: A historical map labelled “1841-map” is held (EV-0005); its survey or edition date is not yet established.

sq.t: c.1841: orchard, meadows and wood farmed
sq.x: The c.1841 tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists “Williams John” as occupier of 36 parcels, about 119½ acres, among them an orchard (no. 211, 1a 3r 19p), meadows and a wood (no. 219, 1a 3r 38p). The landowner listed for 33 of the parcels is the Marquess of Bute.
src: National Library of Wales tithe maps

sq.t: 19th-century Bute estate work on Great House
sq.x: The archaeological report associates 19th-century work on Great House with the Bute Estate; H. S. Corbett, a Bute-associated agent, remodelled Baron's Court around 1850. His role at Great House is not established.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

sq.t: Thomas limeworks at Llandough from 1851
sq.x: People’s Collection Wales records that Daniel Thomas started the limeworks at Llandough in 1851 and that Alfred Thomas continued them; limeworks operated on part of the farm by 1876.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

sq.t: John Williams succeeds father in tenancy, 1855
sq.x: The Cardiff Times (16 July 1904) reported that John Williams “succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855”, calling him “of Llandough Farm”; identification with Great House is an inference (EV-0224).

sq.t: Medieval rowel spur found at Llandough, 1858
sq.x: Museum Wales object 63.24/1, a 14th–15th-century iron rowel spur, was found in 1858 at Llandough Church Farm with six male skeletons during building work. It was displayed in the Museum’s “Origins” gallery until 2014. The record was released with the Museum’s FOI reply on 5 October 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A2 — Museum Wales collections record 63.24/1: medieval iron rowel spur, Llandough Church Farm, 1858

sq.t: Medieval spearhead and spur found at Llandough, c.1858
sq.x: A letter headed Cogan Pill, 22 Nov 1931 (museum file 63.24), records that a spearhead, possibly 15th-century, and a rowel spur “was found a[t] Llandough Church Farm when digging foundations for some new buildings about 1858”, with about six skeletons. Whether Church Farm is Great House Farm is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33 — Amgueddfa Cymru reply to FOI 2026-036 (5 & 7 October 2026): further collections search

sq.t: Spur, spearhead and burials at Church Farm, c.1858
sq.x: The Museum's 1931 letter records a spur and spearhead found at “Llandough Church Farm” about 1858, with about six skeletons reburied south of the church. Whether Church Farm was part of the Great House holding is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: 1864: Amy Williams, widow of Great House, dies
sq.x: Death notices of 30 Dec 1864 recorded that Amy Williams, widow of John Williams of Great House farm, Llandough, died at Llandough on 23 Dec 1864, aged 65.

sq.t: Amy Williams of Great House farm dies, 1864
sq.x: On 23 December 1864 Amy Williams, “relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm”, died at Llandough aged 65 (contemporary press; EV-0246).

sq.t: Archive note: Nancy, daughter of John Williams
sq.x: Glamorgan Archives D/D XJF 64/30–31 holds a note identifying Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm as the daughter of John Williams of Great House Farm (born c. 1867), with her sketch (EV-0155).

sq.t: Directories place John Williams at Great House
sq.x: Trade directories of 1868, 1875, 1880, 1887, 1891 and 1901 list John Williams at “Great House”, Llandough.

sq.t: Armour found under the dining-room floor
sq.x: RCAHMW records (NMR 6048942; Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, NMR 6048944) place an armour find under the farmhouse dining-room floor about 1870; GGAT’s 1990 assessment places it under the rear wing c.1880. HER GGAT02038s records medieval ironwork and pottery reported from the site.

sq.t: c.1870: soldier in armour found under dining room
sq.x: Two Royal Commission archive records describe a find under the farmhouse dining-room floor “in about 1870” of “the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, a lance and shield”; one records that the house “was reputed to be the stable of a Castle” (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974; Coflein 6048942, 6048944).

sq.t: Pwll-y-Pant Williams estate left to Bute, 1870
sq.x: William Evans Williams of Pwll-y-Pant, Caerphilly, a different Williams, died in February 1870 and left his estate to the Marquess of Bute; the 1870 probate of his will is at NLW D242/17.

sq.t: John Williams rated for glebe land, 1872
sq.x: The Llandough poor rate of 9 April 1872 records John Williams rated for glebe land, owner Rev. H. H. Rickards (provisional reading; EV-0212).

sq.t: 1877 lease to John Williams not located
sq.x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams quotes an 1877 lease to John Williams of the Llandough land. That instrument has not been found; Glamorgan Archives’ DBDT/79/1, examined on 14 Sep 2026, is a different counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: 1877 Bute–Thomas deed: no copy found
sq.x: Glamorgan Archives holds no deeds of the 1877 sale of the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas, a Cardiff builder. A library copy of the Bute–Thomas deed was reported missing from Cardiff Library in 1984, the year of BP’s writ.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: Bute serves notice to quit, 1877
sq.x: Mary's statement records that Bute served notice to quit in 1877, then sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas while keeping about 9 acres “up on the top”; her grandfather then held each part from a different landlord.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

sq.t: 1877 Clyde Street lease is not the farm
sq.x: A counterpart lease dated 6 Nov 1877 from the Bute Trustees to “Mr John Williams” is a 99-year building lease of a house plot in Clyde Street, Roath, granted to a builder. It is not a lease of the farm.

sq.t: 1877 lease to John Williams not identified
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement records a lease dated 6 November 1877 to John Williams, but the matching Llandough instrument has not been identified; the physically checked DBDT/79/1 is a 2 May 1877 lease for Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff (SC-20).
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: 6 Nov 1877 deed is a Cardiff lease
sq.x: The deed of 6 November 1877 once linked to the farm is a building lease in Clyde Street, Cardiff; the Llandough instrument of 1877 remains unlocated.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: 1877 promise gave at most an equitable right
sq.x: A promise that the freehold “should belong to my grandfather” when quarrying ceased gave at most a contractual or equitable right; a deed was needed to pass the legal estate (Real Property Act 1845), and an open-ended promise may have been void against later owners (LSWR v Gomm, 1882).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: No Museum accession for c.1880 ironwork
sq.x: The c.1880 “ironwork held by the National Museum” sentence rests on a local tradition; the Museum holds no matching accession and points to the 1858 Church Farm finds (T11.5).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: 1881 census: John Williams at “Llandough Home Farm”
sq.x: The 1881 census records John Williams, 53, “Farmer of 170 [or 120] ac.”, with his wife Mary and children at “Llandough Home Farm”, Llandough (RG11/5288 p.2). Working theory: the census entry refers to Great House Farm under another name (EV-0224).

sq.t: Open-ended land right exposed to perpetuities rule
sq.x: A right to land arising on an uncertain future event with no time limit was vulnerable to the rule against perpetuities as against later owners (London & South Western Railway v Gomm, 1882).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Bute will leaves Leckwith-with-Llandough to Lord Colum
sq.x: The 3rd Marquess of Bute’s will of 30 July 1894, reported in October 1900, named Leckwith-with-Llandough, Michaelston-le-Pit, Cogan, Sully, Lavernock, Penarth and St Andrews among the estates for Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart. The original will is not yet inspected (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

sq.t: Bute’s will leaves Leckwith-with-Llandough estates
sq.x: Newspapers of 18–20 October 1900 reported that the 3rd Marquess of Bute’s will left “all his estates in the parishes of Leckwith, with Llandough” and neighbouring parishes to Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart. The will itself is not yet seen.

sq.t: 1902 Bute auction of Cwm Cydfin Wood
sq.x: Glamorgan Archives file DSA/3/192 records the Marquess of Bute selling coppice woods at auction on 29 Nov 1902, including “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)” and part of Coed-y-Ddylluan.

sq.t: Bute's “Cwm Cydfin Wood” offered at auction, 1902
sq.x: On 29 November 1902 the Marquess of Bute's coppice woods, including “Cwm Cydfin Wood, Leckwith and Llandough”, were offered at auction by Stephenson & Alexander (particular 192; EV-0219).

sq.t: 1904: John Williams, Bute tenant since 1855
sq.x: The Cardiff Times of 16 July 1904 reported Mr John Williams “of Llandough Farm” as a guest at the Marquess of Bute’s rent audit dinner: “He succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855 … Saturday was his 102nd rent audit.” The paper names Llandough Farm, not Great House.

sq.t: Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905
sq.x: A Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905, later held on the WA231076 file and noted on WA735527, dealt with land at the site before registration.

sq.t: 1905 conveyance referred to on title WA231076
sq.x: HM Land Registry title WA231076 refers to a conveyance dated 23 February 1905. Its parties, schedule and plan, and whether it touches Parcel A, are not yet inspected (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

sq.t: Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905
sq.x: A Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905, a deed with Cardiff Corporation, is referred to on the WA231076 first-registration file and burdens part of the later woodland title (EV; not yet held).

sq.t: First-registration files: 1905, 1924, 1961 deeds
sq.x: The WA231076 file holds a 23 February 1905 Bute conveyance granting rights to Cardiff Corporation, a 15 May 1924 agreement and a 29 March 1961 deed. The woodland register records that no copies of the 1905 plans were supplied on first registration.

sq.t: 1905 conveyance likely concerns Parcel B
sq.x: The 1905 Bute conveyance appears to concern rights over land Bute retained and may relate to Parcel B. The 15 May 1924 Bute–Corbett drain agreement may or may not touch Parcel A; neither deed nor plan has yet been inspected.

sq.t: 1877 arrangement placed house estate with Thomas/Williams
sq.x: Working theory: the 1877 arrangement placed the full house and quarrying estate on the Thomas/Williams side and took effect in 1928, so WGR’s 1938 reversion covered only the remaining eastern agricultural fields (Parcel B).
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

sq.t: 1877 Bute–Thomas agreement heads title records
sq.x: The 1877 Bute–Thomas agreement, the Bute counterpart lease and Bute accounts and receipts (GHF-E115 to E117) are the earliest records in the Parcel A title enquiry.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Mary’s statement: freehold to pass when quarrying ceased
sq.x: In her c.1974 statement Mary (Nancy) Williams described an 1877 division: the Bute Estate served notice to quit, sold “the farmhouse and buildings and about 10 acres” to Daniel Thomas and kept “about 9 acres up on the top”; her grandfather rented from both, rent fell as quarrying took land, and the freehold would then pass to him.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Parcel A as the full 1877 house estate
sq.x: Working theory: Parcel A was the full 1877 house and quarrying estate: house, buildings, barn, stable and west-side yard, garden, north forest and the south-east ground later registered as VG41. The farmhouse and garden were only the occupied centre Mary retained.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided

sq.t: Daniel Thomas buys farmhouse, lets to Williams
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement records that in 1877 Daniel Thomas bought the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres from Bute and let them to her grandfather. The original instrument and plan have not been located.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

sq.t: 1877 arrangement: freehold when quarrying ceased
sq.x: Working theory: the 1877 Bute–Thomas arrangement made the end of quarrying and rent in 1928 the trigger for the Williams family to take the freehold of the Parcel A house and quarrying land, distinct from Parcel B, retained by Bute. The original instrument is unavailable.

sq.t: 1877 notice to quit from the Bute Estate
sq.x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams reads: “Prior to 1877 my Grandfather held the farm as tenant of the Bute Family Estates and in that year he received notice to quit from the Bute Estate Office. … he showed me the notice to quit.”
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: Thomas tenancy with “special provisions”
sq.x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams reads: “Daniel Thomas required the farm for quarrying limestone and I remember seeing the tenancy agreement between D. Thomas and my grandfather which contained special provisions with regard to this.”

sq.t: Mary's statement: 1877 Bute–Thomas arrangement
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams's c.1974 statement records an 1877 arrangement in which Bute sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas for quarrying, with the freehold to pass to the Williams family when quarrying ceased. The original deed and plan remain missing.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

sq.t: Statement: freehold to pass when quarrying ceased
sq.x: Mary's statement: “the agreement provided that the rent should progressively decrease as land was taken for quarrying. It was also provided that when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather.” The agreement was kept in the blanket box at the farmhouse.

sq.t: Parcel B: “does not concern this action”
sq.x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams records that the “about 9 acres up on the top” retained by the Bute Estate in 1877 (Parcel B) “was given up later, and does not concern this action”.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

sq.t: Medieval ironwork under the rear wing, c.1880
sq.x: The 1990 archaeological assessment of Great House Farm and Holbrook & Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005), recorded medieval ironwork discovered under the house’s rear wing about 1880 and held by the National Museum of Wales. The Museum’s own records place its Llandough ironwork at Church Farm about 1858.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33 — Amgueddfa Cymru reply to FOI 2026-036 (5 & 7 October 2026): further collections search

sq.t: “Armour” found under rear-wing floor, c. 1880
sq.x: R. F. Suggett’s December 1988 note in HER record GGAT02038s records a report that “armour” was found under the floor of the rear wing at Great House c. 1880.

sq.t: Tree planting and occupation across Parcel A

sq.x: Frederick Buckler held an unwritten yearly tenancy from 1949 of the fields (Parcel B); the married home was the farmhouse (source pending).

sq.t: Mary refuses a tenancy, asserting ownership, 1949
sq.x: In 1949, when Frederick took a new unwritten tenancy, Mary refused a tenancy of the farmhouse, asserting ownership. In April 1974 she told the Daily Telegraph that ownership had been “in dispute for 25 years”.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Surrendered tenancy concerned the fields only
sq.x: The farming, the arrears and the surrendered tenancy all concerned the fields held under the 1939 tenancy (Parcel B). Working theory: John Williams held no tenancy of the house parcel to surrender.

sq.t: Nancy Buckler’s sketch of old Llandough
sq.x: Glamorgan Archives DXJF/64/30 is described as a “Llandough [juxta-Penarth] sketch of former layout of part of village by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm”, dated c.1945–1955.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R52 — Glamorgan Archives email, 11 June 2026

sq.t: Village sketch by Mrs Nancy Buckler, c.1945–55
sq.x: A note and sketch of the old village layout by Mrs Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm names her father as John Williams of Great House Farm, “born about 1867” (Glamorgan Archives D/D XJF 64/30–31; EV-0155).

sq.t: Statement: lodger placed at farm, June 1950
sq.x: Mary's statement records that in June 1950 Mr Knapp, a Penarth estate agent and lay preacher, asked her mother to give accommodation to a man; the man was later imprisoned for theft and told never to return.

sq.t: Lodger placed at the farmhouse, June 1950
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 witness statement names a lodger placed at the farmhouse in June 1950 and records his conviction for theft c. 1951–52. The Penarth petty sessions registers that would confirm it have not yet been searched (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E124 — Penarth petty sessions record: the lodger (Bruce Sutherland), c. 1951–52

sq.t: Working theory: adverse possession against WGR by c.1951
sq.x: Working theory: if the 1939 plan shows WGR's tenancy covered only the fields, adverse possession of the house parcel against WGR from 1938–39 would have completed about 1951, before the 1955 order (A-077).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Limitation against WGR complete about 1951
sq.x: Working theory: any adverse possession of the house against Western Ground Rents ran from 1938–39, not 1955, and would have completed about 1951, before the 1955 order and long before 1962.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Parcel A passes to Mary on father's death
sq.x: On John Williams's death the house parcel (Parcel A) passed to Mary (Nancy) Williams, who with her husband continued to occupy it. No probate or will has yet been traced.

sq.t: 1952: landlords’ agents drop the letting
sq.x: The 1987 judgment records “a letter from the landlords’ agents to their solicitors of October 10 1952 stating that they did not propose to proceed with the letting to Mr Frederick Buckler.”

sq.t: Frederick's last rent payment, 1953
sq.x: Frederick Buckler made his last rent payment for the fields (Parcel B) in 1953.

sq.t: A failed 1954 attempt cannot restart limitation
sq.x: A failed attempt in 1954 to make occupation permissive would not, merely by being proposed, restart a limitation period already completed. The legal effect of the 1955 and 1962 possession orders is a separate question.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: “Whole farm” wording merges Parcels A and B
sq.x: Working theory: the 1955 “whole farm” wording merged Parcel A with Frederick Buckler’s Parcel B agricultural tenancy, and enforcement took the north forest and south-east green along with Parcel B. Mary defended the house, buildings and garden but could not hold the whole Parcel A perimeter (source pending: EV-0032).
src: Legal Wiki: 1955 Parcel-A Loss Dossier — Woodland + VG41 Green

sq.t: 1955 order for the “whole” farm
sq.x: The reported judgment records that the 1955 possession order was for the “whole” farm, and that execution took all parts except the farmhouse and garden.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided

sq.t: WGR sues Frederick alone, “whole of the farm”
sq.x: In 1955 Western Ground Rents sued Frederick Buckler alone in the High Court by summary judgment (Order 14) on his tenancy, using the words “the whole of the farm”. Mary was not a party to the 1955 action.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: 1955 possession order against Frederick Buckler
sq.x: Frederick Buckler’s tenancy was ended by notice on 2 Feb 1955. The High Court then made an Order 14 summary order against him alone for “the whole of the farm”, enforced on 4 July 1955 except for the farmhouse and garden.

sq.t: Possession of “the whole of the farm”
sq.x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment records: “Western Ground Rents then brought proceedings for possession against Mr Frederick Buckler in the High Court and obtained a possession order, under Order 14, in respect of the whole of the farm.”
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Cardiff leases Leckwith Woods for 999 years
sq.x: The Western Mail of 18 March and 28 October 1955 reported that Cardiff held a 176-acre Leckwith Woods, “bought … for a nominal sum in 1942”, with 106 acres leased to the Forestry Commission for 999 years.

sq.t: Working theory: title documents never before the courts
sq.x: Working theory: the documents that decide title to the house parcel, the 1877 agreement, the 1938 conveyance and plan and the 1939 tenancy, were never put before the courts in 1955, 1962, 1974 or 1986–87.
src: Legal Wiki: Fraud & Concealment — the Family’s Case

sq.t: 1955 order: Mary not made a party
sq.x: The 1955 possession order was obtained by summary judgment against Frederick Buckler alone, although Mary (Nancy) Williams, who asserted title, lived in the house. She was not a party.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: “Previous statement” of 1955–62 not held
sq.x: The c.1974 statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams refers to “my previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 possession applications; that earlier statement is not held (EV-0033).
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E127 — Mary (Nancy) Williams’s “previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 applications

sq.t: 1955 order and execution papers unseen
sq.x: The originals of the 1955 possession order and the 4 July 1955 execution papers, and any parcel plan, have not been obtained (GHF-E125, E126); the events are known only through later references. The 1962 pleadings and plan are likewise unseen.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

Legal Wiki: GHF-E126 — 4 July 1955 writ or warrant of possession, execution record and return

sq.t: 1955 “whole farm” possession order executed
sq.x: On 4 July 1955 a High Court possession order obtained by Western Ground Rents, described as covering the “whole farm”, was executed, including the north forest and south-east ground of Parcel A, though the dispute concerned Parcel B (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E126 — 4 July 1955 writ or warrant of possession, execution record and return

sq.t: 4 July 1955: forest and green taken
sq.x: On 4 July 1955, enforcing possession under wording describing the “whole farm”, Western Ground Rents took the forest north of the house and the south-eastern ground later registered as village green VG41. Mary, after a recent leg amputation and with seven children, held the farmhouse, buildings and garden. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Possession taken except farmhouse and garden, 1955
sq.x: The 1987 judgment records that on 4 July 1955 possession was taken of all parts except the farmhouse and garden, an exception attributed to Mary’s recent return from hospital and her strong objection.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: 1955: house spared for Mary’s health, court narrative
sq.x: The court narrative attributes the 1955 decision not to enforce against the farmhouse to Mary’s health and objection, not to the house lying outside the tenancy.
src: Legal Wiki: Fresh Paradigm — Independent Cross-Review of Evidence, Fraud, Concealment & Public Authority Lines (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Northern forest and green seized, 1955
sq.x: Working theory: the 1955 enforcement against the fields of Parcel B also took two parts of Parcel A — the forest north of the house and the ground south-east of it later registered as village green VG41 (source pending).

sq.t: 1955 order enforced on all but farmhouse
sq.x: The 1955 order, summary judgment against Frederick alone for “the whole of the farm”, was enforced on everything except the farmhouse and garden (A-015).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Long silence over land outside the house
sq.x: Long non-challenge over land outside the occupied house can be read against the family as lack of possession, an accepted boundary or acquiescence. Silence does not transfer ownership, but nor does it preserve a title.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: Mary’s “previous statement” of 1955–62 missing
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 statement refers to a “previous statement” she made on the 1955 and 1962 applications. It has not been found on any court file; if it records her assertion of ownership, the other side knew of it by 1955 or 1962.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E127 — Mary (Nancy) Williams’s “previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 applications

sq.t: Bute “allowed her family a slice of land”
sq.x: At the 6 May 1958 Leckwith Common inquiry Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler stated that about 130 years earlier Lord Bute had allowed her family “a slice of land”, a right of way and grazing rights (Western Mail, 7 May 1958).

sq.t: County Council acquires land near Cogan Pill, 1958
sq.x: A Western Mail legal notice of 24 September 1958 recorded a Glamorgan County Council acquisition of land near Cogan Pill, listing Western Ground Rents as owner.

sq.t: 1958 development plan inquiry record unread
sq.x: Days 20–24 of the 1958 public local inquiry into the Glamorgan County Council Development Plan (Area No. 2), 19 November – 11 December 1958, are recorded verbatim at TNA BD 28/177; not yet read (EV-0239).

sq.t: Tenancy offers to Mary, 1959 and 1965
sq.x: Western Ground Rents offered Mary tenancies of the farmhouse and garden in 1959 and 1965. The Court of Appeal’s history records that she refused the 1959 offer and that a later weekly tenancy offer was not signed or returned and no rent was paid.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: WGR offers Mary a farmhouse tenancy, 1959
sq.x: The Court of Appeal records that in 1959 Western Ground Rents offered Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden and that she refused it, asserting ownership through her grandfather (source pending: EV-0039). The original offer and reply are unlocated.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

sq.t: 1961 deed: WGR, Cardiff City and brick company
sq.x: A deed of 29 March 1961 between Western Ground Rents Ltd, “Cardiff City” and South Western Brick & Tile appears on the WA231076 first-registration schedule (GHF-E129).
src: Legal Wiki: Cardiff City Council — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E129 — 29 March 1961 deed: WGR, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City

sq.t: 1961 deed: WGR, brickworks company and Cardiff
sq.x: A deed of 29 March 1961 between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City, recited on woodland title WA735527, affected land now in the woodland title. It is not a Buckler family sale; the land and plan are still to be mapped.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E129 — 29 March 1961 deed: WGR, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City

sq.t: Mary’s “previous statement” missing
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s “previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 applications, referred to in the record, is missing (GHF-E127).

sq.t: Working theory: repeated “permissive” framing of Mary
sq.x: Working theory: repeated efforts to present Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation as permissive (1949, 1959, 1965, 1974), alongside later dealings affecting the woodland and the VG41 ground, weakened or obscured the title to the full Parcel A.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

sq.t: Extent of 1962 order unknown
sq.x: The land covered by the 1962 possession order, and what Mary pleaded in response, are unknown; her “previous statement” is missing (A-014, A-057).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: WGR sells Llandough land to developers, 1962
sq.x: On 5 March 1962 Western Ground Rents conveyed land at Llandough “with other property” to Lakeside and Llandough Development Co Ltd, taking a £75,000 charge; on 11 June 1965 both conveyed a parcel to Glamorgan County Council (Vale FOI reply, 14 September 2026).

sq.t: “No such documents were … ever produced”
sq.x: Mary refused a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden and asserted ownership through her grandfather. The 1987 judgment adds: “No such documents were, however, ever produced” (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: 1962 order on a “one farm” premise
sq.x: Working theory: the 1962 order depended on the farm being one unit as in 1916; the 1924/1928 Parcel A freehold split, the 1938 conveyance and the 1939 tenancy were not, so far as the record shows, put before the court.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

sq.t: Cardiff County Court order, 11 December 1962
sq.x: On 11 December 1962 Cardiff County Court made a possession order against Frederick and Mary concerning the farmhouse and garden (EV-0041, pending).

sq.t: County court possession order for farmhouse, 1962
sq.x: On 11 December 1962 the county court made a possession order for the farmhouse and garden against Frederick and Mary, the remaining occupied house group within Parcel A. The Court of Appeal later treated it as enforceable.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Was the Parcel B plan withheld?
sq.x: Working theory: the landlord’s counterpart of the 1939 tenancy, with its Parcel B plan, passed from WGR to BP. Whether it was shown to the courts in 1955, 1962 or 1984–87 is unknown; presenting a “whole farm” tenancy while holding it would be a misstatement of fact.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: County court registers: arrears, possession, committal
sq.x: Cardiff County Court registers at Glamorgan Archives (ACA, 1953–1975) are catalogued as covering the 1953 arrears action, the 1962 possession order and a 1963 committal.

sq.t: Mesne profits enforced against Frederick, 1963
sq.x: In June 1963 mesne profits were partly enforced against Frederick Buckler under the farmhouse proceedings, with committal proceedings recorded.

sq.t: 1938 conveyance offered as root of title
sq.x: A 1965 contract for the sale of the Llandough school site set special condition F: “Title shall be deduced, and shall commence … with a Conveyance on sale dated 25th December 1938”, making the 1938 conveyance the root of title offered for this Llandough land.

sq.t: 1960s parcel sale (source pending)
sq.x: A recollection records that Frederick’s eldest son sold a land parcel in the 1960s. Which parcel is unknown and no deed has been located (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

sq.t: Weekly tenancy offered again, 1965
sq.x: The Court of Appeal describes a further 1965 offer of a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden. It was not signed or returned, and no rent was paid (EV-0039).
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

sq.t: 1965: WGR refuses to let Frederick the fields
sq.x: In January–March 1965 Frederick Buckler negotiated with Western Ground Rents, which would not let him the agricultural land; the correspondence is recited in the 1987 judgment.

sq.t: Weekly tenancy offered to “Mrs Williams”, 1965
sq.x: On 2 March 1965 the agents of Western Ground Rents offered “Mrs Williams” a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2. It was not signed or returned and no rent was paid; the estate treated her occupation as adverse from then.

sq.t: School land conveyed, 11 June 1965
sq.x: A conveyance of 11 June 1965 between Lakeside and Llandough Development Company Limited, Western Ground Rents Limited and Glamorgan County Council, for £16,800, carried the Llandough Primary School site. Whether the site was ever farm land is open.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

sq.t: Possession order is not a freehold conveyance
sq.x: The 1955 and 1962 possession orders bear on possession, pleadings and occupation. A possession order is not, merely by being made, a conveyance of the freehold; the land covered and legal effect of each order are separate questions.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Clock started 1955 on an assumed tenancy
sq.x: The Court of Appeal started the twelve-year clock on 2 February 1955, the end of Frederick’s tenancy, treating the farmhouse as part of that tenancy. Working theory: WGR’s May 1939 tenancy plan shows Parcel B only, so the farmhouse was never in that tenancy.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Bute granted “a slice of land”, Leckwith Common
sq.x: Western Mail, 7 May 1958, p.7, reported Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler of Great House Farm at the Leckwith Common inquiry: about 130 years earlier Lord Bute allowed her family “a slice of land” which was now Leckwith Common (EV-0035).
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

sq.t: “Have walked in and taken” the land, 1958
sq.x: Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958, p.7, reported Mrs M. D. Buckler (Mary (Nancy) Williams) of Ty Mawr telling the county planning committee that three councils and Western Ground Rents “have walked in and taken” the land, let sites “over her head”, cut off her water for nearly 10 years, and that she lost her Friesian herd.
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

sq.t: 1958 objection: “It’s a Crichel Down”
sq.x: On 20 November 1958 the Western Mail reported Mrs M. D. Buckler objecting to further industrial development near her farm, Ty Mawr, Llandough, and stating that land farmed by her family since 1667 had been “wrongfully appropriated”.

sq.t: “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down”
sq.x: The Western Mail (20 November 1958) reported the evidence of Mary (Nancy) Buckler née Williams that the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents. She told the planning committee: “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down.” (EV-0037).
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: Mary refuses WGR tenancy, asserts ownership, 1959
sq.x: In 1959 Mary (Nancy) Williams refused a Western Ground Rents tenancy of the farmhouse and garden and asserted ownership through her grandfather.

sq.t: Mary repeatedly refused to be a tenant
sq.x: The Court of Appeal’s 1987 account supports that Mary refused the 1959 tenancy offer and asserted ownership; she repeatedly rejected being treated as a tenant and maintained that she was the owner.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

sq.t: 1959: child hurt near Great House Farm home
sq.x: The Western Mail of 27 Nov 1959 reported a five-year-old girl hurt near her home at Great House Farm, Llandough.

sq.t: WGR had to prove its own paper title
sq.x: Working theory: against Mary as an owner-claimant in 1962, Western Ground Rents had to prove its own paper title to Parcel A rather than rely on Frederick’s ended tenancy of the fields.

sq.t: 1962 county court jurisdiction limit
sq.x: County court jurisdiction in December 1962 was limited to property of £100 net annual rateable value, rising to £400 only in 1963. Working theory: if the farmhouse exceeded £100, the order was made without jurisdiction; the 1956 and 1963 valuation lists would test this.

sq.t: Three skeletons found in utility trench, 1963
sq.x: Three skeletons were reported found in utility-trench works at the site in 1963 (secondary research-file account; the 1963 record is awaited).

sq.t: Mary refuses £2 weekly tenancy, 1965
sq.x: On 2 March 1965 Mary refused a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2 offered to “Mrs Williams”; nothing was signed, no rent paid, and the estate treated her occupation as adverse from then (WGR agents' letter recited in the 1987 judgment, GHF-E009-18).

sq.t: Frederick Buckler dies, 1967
sq.x: Frederick Buckler died in 1967; Mary continued “in occupation of the farmhouse and land surrounding it”.

sq.t: Frederick Buckler dies, 1967; Mary stays on
sq.x: Mary stated: “I am a widow, my husband Frederick Buckler having died in the year 1967”. He was 56. Mary then returned to her maiden name and continued in occupation of the farmhouse.

sq.t: WGR conveys to BP Pension Trust, 1969
sq.x: In 1969 Western Ground Rents conveyed its interest to BP Pension Trust. The conveyance has not been retrieved; the 1987 judgment treats the sale as including the farmhouse and garden (EV-0043, pending).

sq.t: 1969 root of title missing from both files
sq.x: Both BP conveyances recite a 31 December 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust as their root of title; it is not on either file's schedule. The 1987 judgment records the 23 May 1975 conveyance as “the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden”.
src: Legal Wiki: Western Ground Rents Ltd
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust

sq.t: BP Pension Trust buys from WGR, 1969
sq.x: On 31 December 1969 BP Pension Trust bought from Western Ground Rents. The deed is not on HM Land Registry’s first-registration schedule (GHF-E131).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E131 — 31 December 1969 WGR to BP Pension Trust conveyance (root of title), with plan

sq.t: Conveyances to BP Pension Trust and BP Properties
sq.x: Between 1969 and 1975 Western Ground Rents conveyed to BP Pension Trust, and BP Pension Trust to BP Properties, describing the land together. The 1969 root deed and the 1971 abstract are absent from HM Land Registry’s 2026 schedule.

sq.t: Interest passes to BP Pension Trust, then BP Properties (our case: Parcel B and an interest in the 1962 order on Parcel A in 1969)
sq.x: Later instruments recite a 31 Dec 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust. A 23 May 1975 conveyance from BP Pension Trust to BP Properties is linked with the farmhouse title WA240304. The exact parcels are not yet proved.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

sq.t: 1969 root deed and 1971 abstract missing
sq.x: Later documents recite a 31 Dec 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust and a 1971 abstract of title, but HM Land Registry’s 30 July 2026 schedule does not list either as surviving on the registration files.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Site ground registered as village green VG41
sq.x: Part of the site by Leckwith Road was provisionally registered as village green VG41 on 16 June 1970 under the Commons Registration Act 1965; the current reconstruction places it within Parcel A. The VG41 ownership file records who asserted ownership of that land around 1970–80.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Village green VG41 registered, 1970
sq.x: Village green VG41 was provisionally registered on 16 June 1970 under the Commons Registration Act 1965, whose registers had an ownership section; unclaimed land could be vested in the local authority (s.8). Who asserted ownership, and on what evidence, is not yet shown (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

sq.t: 1971 abstract of title not on the file
sq.x: Later instruments recite a 1971 abstract of title for BP Pension Trust, but it is not a free-standing item on the HM Land Registry file. It is the best single record of the root BP’s side relied on, and its whereabouts are unknown.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E132 — 1971 abstract of title (BP Pension Trust)

sq.t: 1972 permission for about 13 houses
sq.x: In 1972 BP Pension Trust obtained outline permission 3/8996/3337 for about 13 houses on the farm land while Mary (Nancy) Williams occupied the house and disputed ownership. No archaeological condition was attached; the ownership certificate has not yet been obtained.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E134 — 1972 outline planning permission 3/8996/3337 (about 13 houses) and ownership certificate

sq.t: Planning permission for 13 houses, 1972
sq.x: In 1972 BP Pension Trust obtained planning permission for about 13 houses (3/8996/3337) while Mary occupied the house and disputed ownership. Applications then needed an ownership certificate naming every owner (Town and Country Planning Act 1962 s.16); the 1972 certificate is unseen.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Housing permission on the site, 25 Jul 1972
sq.x: The 1989 planning officer’s report records a housing permission on the site dated 25 July 1972, granted while Mary (Nancy) Williams still occupied the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: 31 Jul 1972: VG41 objection period ends
sq.x: The second objection period under the Commons Registration Act 1965 ends on 31 July 1972. It covers village green VG41, provisionally registered on 16 June 1970; notice of it was given by public notice only.

sq.t: 1877 terms rest on childhood memory
sq.x: The 1877 terms rest on Mary's memory of a document she saw as a child, and the account of papers being taken is second-hand. Her statement was made c.1974, before the litigation, and the 1974 press record matches it.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

sq.t: 1974 BP letters treated as licence
sq.x: Letters from BP Properties Ltd in 1974 were later held by the Court of Appeal to operate as a licence, changing the legal character of the possession of Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust
Legal Wiki: GHF-E137 — 1974 H. J. Thomas architectural survey and floor plan (RCAHMW / National Monuments Record)

sq.t: Mary pleads ownership; BP revives 1962 order
sq.x: BP Pension Trust sued Mary in 1974; on 3 July 1974 the action was adjourned part heard for a defence, which pleaded the Limitation Act 1939. The action stalled and BP revived the 1962 order instead. Licence letters followed on 31 October 1974, one from BP Properties, which then held only a contract to buy.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: 1974 action, enforcement and licence letters
sq.x: The record refers to a July 1974 possession action with an ownership plea, leave to enforce in September, a warrant not before 31 October, and licence letters dated 31 October 1974.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: September 1974 enforcement order
sq.x: A September 1974 enforcement order was made against the occupation. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s solicitors challenged it on notice grounds; the appeal notice, order and outcome are not yet seen (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Leave to enforce the 1962 order, 1974
sq.x: On 19 September 1974 the county court gave BP leave to enforce the possession order of 11 December 1962, with no warrant before 31 October. Mary’s solicitors appealed because she had not been given notice; the stay application came before the judge on 4 November, and the landlords’ solicitors then withdrew the warrant, at a date before 25 November 1974.

sq.t: Leave to enforce 1962 order; warrant withdrawn
sq.x: On 19 September 1974 leave was obtained to enforce the 1962 possession order; the warrant was withdrawn later, at a date before 25 November 1974 (after the licence letters of 31 October and the hearing of 4 November).

sq.t: Working theory: 1974 steps timed before a deadline
sq.x: Working theory: if the 1962 order reset the limitation clock, 11 Dec 1974 would have been a twelve-year deadline, and the October 1974 enforcement steps and licence letters were clustered just before it. The 1974 pleadings and judgments would test this.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: 1974 licence letter from a not-yet-owner
sq.x: The second letter of 31 Oct 1974 came from BP Properties, which held only a contract to buy until the May 1975 conveyance, after BP Pension Trust’s action stalled on the ownership plea of Mary (Nancy) Williams.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

sq.t: 1974 licence letters: possession recast as licence
sq.x: BP letters dated 31 Oct 1974, covering the central house and garden, were later treated by the Court of Appeal as placing Mary’s continued possession under a licence, which was material to the limitation outcome.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute

sq.t: BP: rent-free “because of her ill health”
sq.x: In 1974 BP stated it allowed Mary to stay rent-free “because of her ill health”; she was a widow and an amputee in a wheelchair. The Court of Appeal held the letters made her possession permissive although she never accepted them.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Licence letters offer farmhouse occupation, 1974
sq.x: Letters of 31 October 1974 (addressed to “Mary Buckler” on the family copy, SOURCE PENDING; described by the Court of Appeal as to “Mrs Buckler (described again as Mrs Williams)”) offered a licence to stay in the farmhouse. The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment relied on this licence (GHF-E136; EV-0080). Whether the letters identified the land later registered to BP is not established.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Licence letters: “rent free”, 31 Oct 1974
sq.x: BP’s letters of 31 October 1974 offered Mary a licence to stay in the farmhouse; the landlords’ solicitors withdrew the warrant later, at a date before 25 November 1974. In 1988 the press reported BP’s version: “In 1974 BP Properties agreed to allow Mrs Buckler to remain in the farmhouse rent free”, “because of her ill health”.
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: BP licence letters to “Mary Buckler” (family copy)
sq.x: On 31 October 1974 BP sent licence letters. The family copy is addressed to “Mary Buckler” (image SOURCE PENDING); the 1987 Court of Appeal describes them as addressed to “Mrs Buckler (described again as Mrs Williams)”. They were never accepted (EV-0050, pending).

sq.t: Licence offered before BP Properties held title
sq.x: The first 31 October 1974 letter, from BP Pension Trust, recorded an agreed sale to BP Properties; the second, from BP Properties, offered the licence. BP Properties did not take a conveyance until May 1975 (court record).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Working theory: a reconstructed “whole farm” parcel
sq.x: Working theory: a later document or composite parcel was used to reconstruct a “whole farm” description without the genuine documentary chain for the house plot. To be proved or disproved from the conveyances, plans and register history.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Two dates for the 1975 conveyance plan
sq.x: HM Land Registry file WA240304 lists item 13 as a “Plan to conveyance dated 23 February 1975”, while item 1 and every other record give 23 May 1975. Whether this is a typing slip or a second instrument is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: 1975 conveyance: BP Pension Trust to BP Properties
sq.x: On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveyed the farmhouse and garden to BP Properties, the first conveyance into the company that had issued the October 1974 licence. Title WA240304 was later registered on it; its plan (item 13) is dated 23 February 1975.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E138 — 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust to BP Properties conveyance and plan (WA240304 items 1, 12, 13)

sq.t: BP Pension Trust conveys to BP Properties, 1975
sq.x: On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveyed land to BP Properties Ltd by a deed and plan later relied on for the farmhouse-and-garden first registration, title WA240304. The deed shows what it purported to convey, not that the transferor held every part.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake
Legal Wiki: GHF-E138 — 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust to BP Properties conveyance and plan (WA240304 items 1, 12, 13)

sq.t: BP Pension Trust conveys to BP Properties, 1975
sq.x: On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveyed to BP Properties Ltd; the 1987 judgment records it as “the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden”.

sq.t: Conflicting 1975 conveyance date on file
sq.x: Item 13 on the WA240304 schedule is dated “23 February 1975”; every other record dates the BP Pension Trust to BP Properties conveyance 23 May 1975.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Registration certificate of “undisputed possession”
sq.x: Compulsory registration of title began in the Vale of Glamorgan on 1 Dec 1975. The solicitor’s certificate form for a first registration states belief that the applicant “is and has been in undisputed possession or in receipt of rents and profits” and knows of nothing “adverse to the applicant”. The February 1983 wording itself is unseen.

sq.t: 1994 burials not shown on Parcel A
sq.x: GGAT’s 1978–79 excavation was of the Llandough Roman Villa south of the church, not Great House Farm, and it has not been shown that the 1994 burials lay on Parcel A.

sq.t: Llandough Farm is a separate farmstead
sq.x: Records naming “Great House”, “Ty Mawr” or “Llandough” are not all about this farm: Llandough Farm, south of the church, was a separate farmstead on the Roman villa site, built over for housing in 1978–79; Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge is a different parish.

sq.t: House only partially recorded “because of ownership dispute”
sq.x: The Royal Commission’s own archive records that the house remained only partially recorded because of an ownership dispute.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry
Legal Wiki: Where Things Stand — October 2026

sq.t: Later good-faith buyers are protected
sq.x: Limitation Act 1980 s.32(3) protects a later purchaser for valuable consideration who was not party to any fraud, as does the priority rule for registered land. This bears on any remedy concerning the woodland.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: BP pension fund buys Western Ground Rents
sq.x: Hansard recorded in May 1980 that Western Ground Rents had been bought by the BP pension fund.
src: Legal Wiki: Companies House — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Possible gap in the chain to Parcel A
sq.x: Working theory: if the 1938 conveyance did not include Parcel A and no other instrument conveyed it to Western Ground Rents, the December 1969 deed to BP Pension Trust would carry a material gap in the chain for Parcel A.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Cwm Cydfin wood notified as SSSI
sq.x: Cwm Cydfin, Leckwith, “a mixed deciduous woodland adjacent to saltings of the River Ely” of 5.5 ha (ST 165739), was notified as a Site of Special Scientific Interest in 1972 and re-notified on 9 Dec 1985.

sq.t: Cwm Cydfin notified as SSSI, 1972
sq.x: In 1972 Cwm Cydfin, Leckwith, was notified as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI 0524; EV-0218).

sq.t: 1974 architectural survey of the house
sq.x: H. J. Thomas’s 1974 survey and floor plan, held by RCAHMW (National Monuments Record), documented a sub-medieval or late-seventeenth-century building. RCAHMW records that the house was only partly recorded because of the ownership dispute. The related Johns–Buckler correspondence has been lost “since 1986/87”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E137 — 1974 H. J. Thomas architectural survey and floor plan (RCAHMW / National Monuments Record)

sq.t: 1974 survey noted historic features, possible medieval core
sq.x: The regional Historic Environment Record entry GGAT02038s cites R. F. Suggett’s December 1988 note and H. J. Thomas’s 1974 survey of the house, which recorded historic architectural features and considered a possible medieval core.
src: Legal Wiki: European Commission of Human Rights / Strasbourg — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams, c.1974
sq.x: Her witness statement (c.1974) reads: “My family have lived and farmed at Great House Farm since 1667.” “It was also provided that when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather.” “I have never … paid rent to or acknowledged the title of anyone as landlord.”
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

sq.t: Farmhouse opened to the public, 1974
sq.x: On 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams, then 60, opened the farmhouse “to show what the nation is losing”, and hundreds came. About 1,000 people had signed a petition. “My family has lived here for more than 400 years” (EV-0048).

sq.t: Mary opens farmhouse to the public, 1974
sq.x: On 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams opened the farmhouse to the public “to show what the nation is losing”; a petition gathered about 1,000 signatures (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: Open day to save Tŷ Mawr, 1974
sq.x: The Daily Telegraph reported that on 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams held a public open day at Ty Mawr against planned demolition: “The ownership of the house has been in dispute for 25 years but my family has lived here for more than 400 years.”

sq.t: 1974 H. J. Thomas architectural survey
sq.x: RCAHMW holds the H. J. Thomas survey material for Great House Farm, including a 1974 architectural survey and floor plan documenting a sub-medieval / late-seventeenth-century building, with related photographs.

sq.t: 1974 investigator’s notes and sketch plan
sq.x: RCAHMW record NMR 6048943 holds H. J. Thomas’s 1974 investigator’s notes on Great House Farm, with a sketch plan of the building.

sq.t: Mary pleads ownership in court, 1974
sq.x: On 3 July 1974 the action was adjourned part heard for a formal defence; Mary’s defence then pleaded ownership under the Limitation Act 1939. It was never relisted; BP instead revived the 1962 order and sent the licence letters.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Plea of ownership in county court, 1974
sq.x: In BP Pension Trust’s county-court action, adjourned part heard on 3 July 1974, Mary (Nancy) Williams pleaded in her defence that she owned the house (EV-0049). The pleadings are not yet obtained.
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E135 — 3 July 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams’s plea of ownership and the pleadings in BP Pension Trust’s county-court action

sq.t: Vaughan phase, Bute works and medieval pottery
sq.x: GGAT linked the seventeenth-century phase of the house to the Vaughan family and nineteenth-century work to the Bute Estate. Features were recorded in situ in 1974, others in the rubble, and twelfth- to fourteenth-century pottery sherds were recovered by E. J. Beare.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

sq.t: Ownership on record years before the litigation
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement dates from about 1974, over a decade before the 1986–87 litigation. A 1974 newspaper report records her ownership position and a lawyer’s view that she had a case; William Buckler’s 1983 diary records the Daniel Thomas receipts.
src: Legal Wiki: Anticipated Objections and the Family’s Answers

sq.t: 1974 licence letters covered house and garden only
sq.x: The 1974 licence letters applied to the farmhouse and garden. Working theory: a ruling on those letters does not decide the woodland or the green land, if a separate documentary title to them is shown.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: Letter “Grievous loss” against demolition
sq.x: A letter by William Rees headed “Grievous loss” appeared in the Western Mail on 19 November (year unclear, 1970s), opposing demolition of the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: William Rees: Tŷ Mawr “the manorhouse of Llandough”
sq.x: A Western Mail letter signed “William Rees, Penarth” opposed demolition of Great House Farm, describing the farmstead of Great House, or Ty Mawr, as “serving as the manorhouse of Llandough” (GHF-E090-N04; year of the cutting unclear).

sq.t: 1980 talk: Roman villa, medieval house at Llandough
sq.x: The Neath Guardian of 17 April 1980 reported a talk by the assistant director of the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust on recent digs at Llandough, where substantial remains of a Roman villa and “part of a later medieval house” were found. The report did not locate the medieval house.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980)

sq.t: 1980: Trust excavates at Llandough
sq.x: The Neath Guardian of 17 April 1980 reported a talk by the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust’s assistant director on its work, including excavations at Llandough near Cardiff, in the separate Roman-villa context.
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — 17 April 1980: “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980)

sq.t: Hansard 1980: BP fund criticised as ground landlord
sq.x: In the Commons on 22 May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP stated that Western Ground Rents had been bought by the BP pension fund and that the fund was behaving harshly towards householders as a ground landlord. The debate did not name Great House Farm.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N16 — House of Commons, 22 May 1980: Ted Rowlands MP on BP and Western Ground Rents (Hansard)

sq.t: Hansard: Ted Rowlands MP on BP, 1980
sq.x: On 22 May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP raised BP and Western Ground Rents in the House of Commons, as recorded in Hansard (GHF-E090-N16).
src: Legal Wiki: House of Lords — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N16 — House of Commons, 22 May 1980: Ted Rowlands MP on BP and Western Ground Rents (Hansard)

sq.t: GGAT warning and Land Registry registration, 1982–85
sq.x: Between 1982 and 1985 an early GGAT archaeological warning about the site was recorded, while HM Land Registry registration of the land proceeded.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: HM Land Registry — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Woodland title built from two strands
sq.x: Woodland title WA735527 contains land tinted blue, from the 1975 farmhouse conveyance, and land tinted pink, from a 1982 conveyance subject to Bute’s 1905 deed with Cardiff Corporation and Western Ground Rents’ 1961 deed. Only the blue part follows the farmhouse strand.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: No action for 2,258 days after 1982 warning
sq.x: No institutional action is recorded for 2,258 days after GGAT's own archaeological warning of 1 October 1982 (GGAT report T3).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Development assessed at Tŷ Mawr Farm, 1982
sq.x: HER record GGAT02038s records an October 1982 GGAT assessment and consultation concerning Tŷ Mawr Farm (H2.1) and archaeological investigation before development, while the farmhouse was still occupied.

sq.t: Judgment: BP owned “the whole” farm since 1982
sq.x: The published judgment states that BP had paper title and had been registered proprietor of “the whole” farm since November 1982, while two separate titles (WA231076 and WA240304) were live until the 1987 amalgamation (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: Court of Appeal — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Conveyance of 19 Nov 1982 behind WA231076
sq.x: HM Land Registry’s registration history records that the first registration of WA231076 (applied for 30 November 1982) relied on a conveyance dated 19 November 1982, and WA240304 (23 February 1983) on a conveyance dated 23 May 1975.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: BP applies for first registration during occupation
sq.x: In 1982–83 BP applied for first registration of titles WA231076 and WA240304 while Mary (Nancy) Williams was in occupation (EV-0065, pending).

sq.t: HM Land Registry first registration to BP, 1982–83
sq.x: HM Land Registry first registered the relevant Great House Farm land to BP in 1982/83, while Mary (Nancy) Williams was still living at the house.

sq.t: “Mrs Williams” and “Mrs Buckler” name mismatch
sq.x: Records use both “Mrs Williams” and “Mrs Buckler” for the occupier. Working theory: the mismatch may have impeded notice to the actual occupier at first registration.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: First registration of main site, Nov 1982
sq.x: First registration of the main site, title WA231076, was applied for on 30 November 1982; the title is now registered to Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd. The instrument carrying the farmhouse and garden into it has not been identified.

sq.t: No notice to occupier of first registration
sq.x: First registration of the land in 1982–83 took place while the family was in occupation, with no evidence that the occupier was given notice or an effective opportunity to object.

sq.t: First registration to BP while Mary lived there
sq.x: HM Land Registry’s first registration placed Great House Farm land in BP’s registered ownership in 1982–83 while the occupier still lived at the farmhouse. Notice of the registration was first seen after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, during the mourning period.
src: Legal Wiki: 1982–83 Registration & Opportunity to Object

sq.t: Two separate first-registration strands
sq.x: The land entered the register in two strands: WA231076, the earlier strand for the fields (Parcel B), and WA240304, the later farmhouse-and-garden strand relying on the 23 May 1975 conveyance (source pending: EV-0052).
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Returned deeds are not proof of concealment
sq.x: HM Land Registry normally returned original deeds and abstracts to applicants after first registration, so the absence of the 1969 conveyance and 1971 abstract from the file is not by itself evidence of concealment.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Solicitors certify “no question or doubt” on title
sq.x: At first registration BP’s solicitors, Linklaters, certified that they knew of “no question or doubt affecting the title”. Mary had pleaded ownership and limitation in court in 1974, and that plea was never withdrawn or decided.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Farmhouse title WA240304 registered, Feb 1983
sq.x: The farmhouse-and-garden title WA240304, based on the 23 May 1975 conveyance, was applied for on 23 February 1983, later amalgamated into WA231076 and closed.

sq.t: First-registration application, 23 Feb 1983
sq.x: HM Land Registry file WA240304 item 10 is the register and first-registration application of 23 February 1983, made a month before Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983.

sq.t: 1983 certificate: “no question or doubt” on title
sq.x: Linklaters applied for the farmhouse title WA240304 on 23 February 1983 and certified they knew of no question or doubt affecting title, though Mary's 1974 plea of ownership had never been decided. Working theory: this omission is material.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Farmhouse title WA240304 applied for, Feb 1983
sq.x: On 23 Feb 1983 Linklaters applied to register the farmhouse-and-garden title WA240304 on the May 1975 conveyance, certifying no question or doubt affecting title, while the 1974 plea of ownership by Mary (Nancy) Williams was undecided. She died on 26 March 1983.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

sq.t: First registrations WA231076 and WA240304, 1982–83
sq.x: First registration of title WA231076 was applied for on 30 Nov 1982 and of WA240304, the farmhouse title, on 23 Feb 1983. The files hold correspondence of April and May 1983, after Mary’s death, and a new register edition of 13 Jan 1984.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Working theory: 1983 registration left out Mary’s title
sq.x: Working theory: BP registered the house parcel in 1983 without disclosing that Mary (Nancy) Williams asserted ownership; the separate documentary root of Parcel A was never reconciled with the registered titles, and the titles were merged in 1987.
src: Legal Wiki: Fraud & Concealment — the Family’s Case

sq.t: Working theory: a synthetic Parcel A registered
sq.x: Working theory: the 1982–83 registrations WA231076 and WA240304 created a registered plot that mimicked the historic Parcel A centre, without an independent root of title, and it was later combined with Parcel B. The original applications, deeds and plans would decide this.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute

sq.t: Working theory: a gap became a title fact
sq.x: Working theory: a gap in the documentary chain to Parcel A was converted into an apparent title fact by registration and by repeated later description. Whether that was accidental, negligent, misleading or fraudulent is unproved.
src: Legal Wiki: Fresh Paradigm — Independent Cross-Review of Evidence, Fraud, Concealment & Public Authority Lines (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Fire destroys Trust’s excavation finds, 1983
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 18 March 1983 reported that a fire at the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust’s Swansea warehouse destroyed excavation finds, including Llandough Roman villa material; about 90% was unrecoverable.

sq.t: Working theory: 1983 registration notice came too late
sq.x: Working theory: notice connected with the 1983 first registration arrived only after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, so she never had the chance to object. The original notice and proof of dispatch are not yet found. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm: Case Overview and Key Records
Legal Wiki: GHF-E180 — Reported HMLR notification after Mary (Nancy) Williams’s death (original pending)

sq.t: Notice of registration after Mary’s death
sq.x: Working theory: notice of the registration reached the occupying family only after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, leaving her no practical window to object (source pending).

sq.t: Linklaters–HMLR correspondence after Mary's death
sq.x: On 8 and 12 April 1983 Linklaters and HM Land Registry corresponded on the farmhouse title WA240304, including form D23 “inside exam”, after Mary (Nancy) Williams's death (EV-0069, EV-0070, pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: April 1983 registration correspondence not obtained
sq.x: The April 1983 correspondence on the farmhouse title file, written after Mary's death, has not been obtained (GHF-E026-27).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Linklaters letters on registration files, 1983
sq.x: The HM Land Registry file schedule records multiple Linklaters & Paines letters, including correspondence of 12 May 1983, connected with titles WA240304 and WA231076. Linklaters acted for BP in the 1984–87 litigation.

sq.t: BP serves writ on William Buckler, 1984
sq.x: After Mary died on 26 March 1983, her son William Buckler inherited her estate and stayed at the farm. On 22 May 1984 BP served him with a writ for possession of Great House Farm and adjoining land.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
