sq.t: BP writ for possession, 22 May 1984
sq.x: On 22 May 1984 BP Properties Ltd issued a writ for possession of the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Cardiff Library copy of Bute–Thomas deed
sq.x: A Cardiff Library copy of the 1877 Bute–Thomas deed and its index card, relevant around BP's writ for possession of 22 May 1984, has not been located (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Bute–Thomas deed copy vanishes from library, 1984
sq.x: In 1984, the year BP served its writ, a copy of the Bute–Thomas deed and its index card were found missing from Cardiff Library.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

sq.t: Record losses cluster around proceedings
sq.x: Working theory: losses of records cluster around legal proceedings: c.1950–52 before the 1955 action, 1984 at the writ, and 1986/87 at trial and appeal. Explanations are being sought from the record-holders (A-078).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: “Whole farm” description conflated Parcels A and B
sq.x: Working theory: the 1986–87 limitation and licence findings were applied to a conflated “whole farm” description that masked the distinction between Parcel A and Parcel B and the 1955 seizure of the Parcel A forest and green. Mary asserted ownership before the 1984 writ.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Defence counted from 1955 on “whole farm”
sq.x: The defence counted adverse possession from the 1955 enforcement using the “whole farm” description. Working theory: this later starting point obscured the 1928 title effect and the taking of Parcel A forest and green during enforcement against Parcel B.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm — The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature

sq.t: RCAHMW–Mrs Buckler correspondence missing since 1986
sq.x: Correspondence between C. N. Johns of RCAHMW and Mrs Buckler (NMR 6048945) has been missing since 1986/87, the years of the High Court trial and appeal (RCAHMW, 10 June 2026).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: High Court judgment for BP, 24 Jul 1986
sq.x: Mr Justice Hollis heard the case on 10 July 1986 and gave judgment on 24 July 1986. He held that the 1974 letters gave Mary a valid licence, so she was not in adverse possession. Judgment was for BP, the possession order suspended for six months (South Wales Echo, 25 July 1986).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: High Court judgment for BP, 24 July 1986
sq.x: After a hearing on 10 July 1986 before Hollis J, the High Court gave judgment for BP on 24 July 1986, suspending possession for six months (South Wales Echo, 25 July 1986; EV-0074, pending).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Possessory case for rest of farm failed
sq.x: The Court of Appeal noted that the possessory-title case for the remainder of the farm had failed at first instance, the acts relied on being found too tenuous and equivocal, and that part of the possession order was not challenged on appeal.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: 1986 trial lost; 1987 appeal dismissed
sq.x: In 1986 Hollis J in the High Court rejected the adverse-possession defence, finding Frederick lacked the intention to possess. In 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ) disagreed on intention but dismissed the appeal on the basis of the 1962 order and the 1974 letters.
src: Legal Wiki: High Court — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Leave to appeal to House of Lords refused
sq.x: The 1987 Court of Appeal report records: “Leave to appeal to the House of Lords was refused but a stay pending a possible application to the House was granted on terms.” A petition for leave to the House of Lords followed (EV-0080, GHF-E142).
src: Legal Wiki: House of Lords — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: 1987 appeal and HMLR amalgamation during it
sq.x: The Court of Appeal decided BP Properties Ltd v Buckler in 1987 on the 1974 letters and licence issue. HM Land Registry amalgamated titles during the appeal.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)

sq.t: 1987: BP “registered proprietors” since 1982
sq.x: The 1987 appeal was “limited to the farmhouse itself and its garden”. The court recited that BP “have the paper title to the farm, and indeed since November 1982 they have been the registered proprietors”, found Frederick and Mary in adverse possession from February 1955, but held title not extinguished because of the 1962 order and 1974 licence.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Title documents “never produced” in 1987
sq.x: The 1987 court recorded that Mary's title documents were “never produced”, without knowing why. Mary (Nancy) Williams stated in her c.1974 witness statement that they were taken in 1950–52 (F1; A-058).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

sq.t: Mary's ownership case was before the court
sq.x: Mary's ownership case was recited to the Court of Appeal in 1987, so it was not hidden from that court; the court never saw the plans or papers relied on for it.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Amalgamation applied for while appeal pending
sq.x: Two title numbers (WA231076 and WA240304) remained live after the 1986 trial, and an amalgamation application is dated 2 February 1987 while the appeal was pending (source pending: EV-0078). Two title numbers do not by themselves prove different ownership.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Title amalgamation applied for during appeal
sq.x: On 2 February 1987 an application to amalgamate the farmhouse and main-site titles was made while the appeal was still live.
src: Legal Wiki: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal

sq.t: Titles amalgamated during the appeal, 1987
sq.x: An application to amalgamate the registered titles was made on 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler was live. Its exact legal and spatial effect is unproved. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Titles amalgamated while appeal was open, 1987
sq.x: HM Land Registry’s history records two titles: WA231076 (applied for 30 Nov 1982) and WA240304 (23 Feb 1983, the farmhouse-and-garden title), both live at the judgment of 24 July 1986. Amalgamation was applied for on 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal was open, and WA240304 closed.

sq.t: Local Plan: retain buildings; no preservation notice
sq.x: The East Vale Local Plan (February 1987) stated the buildings on the site should be retained. The Council had power to serve a building preservation notice (Town and Country Planning Act 1971, s.58); no notice was served.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Court finds a tenancy without written agreement
sq.x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment concluded that “even though there was no written agreement, Mr Frederick Buckler had a periodic tenancy which was protected by the Agricultural Holdings Act.”

sq.t: 1987 defence knew of the separate 1975 conveyance
sq.x: In 1987 William’s side argued, as its “third argument”, that the farmhouse came under its own May 1975 conveyance. The lawyers therefore knew of the separate conveyance during the litigation, which weakens a later argument that the 1983 registration could not have been discovered.

sq.t: 1987: council drops farm right-of-way application
sq.x: Llandough Community Council minutes of 1987 record “RIGHT OF WAY FROM GREAT HOUSE FARM TO THE SWISS COTTAGES … there is no justification for the right of way being submitted … no further action.” The minutes name Debenham Tewson as “the agents for BP Properties” and record a licence fee paid to them.

sq.t: No grant of representation to Mary's estate
sq.x: The 1987 Court of Appeal report records that no grant of representation to the estate of Mary (Nancy) Williams had been obtained by July 1987. Solicitors: Loosemores for Mr Buckler; Linklaters & Paines for BP Properties.

sq.t: Court of Appeal dismisses appeal, 31 Jul 1987
sq.x: On 31 July 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ, with Mustill LJ and Sir Edward Eveleigh agreeing) gave judgment for BP Properties Ltd in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal

sq.t: Court of Appeal dismisses appeal, 31 July 1987
sq.x: On 31 July 1987 the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Court of Appeal judgment, 31 Jul 1987
sq.x: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2, 31 July 1987: the appeal of William (Billy) Buckler, limited to the farmhouse and garden, was decided against him (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E141 — 31 July 1987 Court of Appeal judgment: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

sq.t: Court of Appeal: “whole” farm, registered proprietor
sq.x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment described Bute’s 1916 grant as an agricultural tenancy of the “whole” farm, the 1938 reversion as conveyed to Western Ground Rents, and BP as registered proprietor from November 1982.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

sq.t: “Might have been different” limited to licence point
sq.x: The 1987 appeal judgment’s remark that the result might have been different concerned Mary expressly repudiating the 1974 licence letters. It is not a finding that a full trial of the 1877 root title would have produced a different result.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: 1974 letters made possession “permissive” regardless
sq.x: The Court of Appeal held that BP’s 1974 letters made Mary’s possession permissive whether or not she accepted them.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided

sq.t: “No such documents were, however, ever produced”
sq.x: The appeal judgment records of Mary’s title papers: “No such documents were, however, ever produced.” Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c. 1974 statement records that the title deed and papers went missing in 1950–52.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

sq.t: Court recites BP’s “paper title” as background
sq.x: In 1984–87 the defence argued adverse possession only. The Court of Appeal recited BP’s “paper title” as background and recorded that Mary’s title documents were “never produced”.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Judgment: Mary “conceived the notion” of ancestral title
sq.x: The 1987 judgment describes Mary as having “conceived the notion” of ancestral title and records that she did not produce the documents. The published reasons do not establish whether the 1877 transaction vested Parcel A in the Williams family.
src: Legal Wiki: Court of Appeal — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: A chain of “whole farm” descriptions
sq.x: Working theory: each adverse step relies on the one before describing the land as “the farm” or “the whole farm”: the 1916 tenancy, the 1955 and 1962 orders, the 1969 and 1975 conveyances, the 1982–83 registration, the 1987 judgment. No independent conveyance of the house parcel into that chain has been seen.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Farm roadway called “an unofficial access route”
sq.x: Council minutes of 17 December 1987 record a resident's request for VG41 to be “extended up to the farm wall” and describe the farm roadway as “an unofficial access route” (EV-0214).

sq.t: Possible lack of proper care at first registration
sq.x: Working theory: if BP or its agent applied to register the house plot despite an excluding conveyance, or without bringing the occupied plot and its occupier to the Registrar’s attention, that could have caused or contributed to a registration mistake.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: 1982 warning on the farm’s archaeological sensitivity
sq.x: On 1 Oct 1982 the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust wrote a letter warning of Great House Farm’s archaeological sensitivity. The recipient and any reply are not known. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E139 — 1 October 1982 GGAT warning about Great House Farm

sq.t: GGAT warning about Great House Farm, 1982
sq.x: On 1 October 1982, weeks before the first registration application, the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust issued a warning about Great House Farm (GHF-E139).
src: Legal Wiki: Welsh Government — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E139 — 1 October 1982 GGAT warning about Great House Farm

sq.t: GGAT warns of archaeological sensitivity, 1982
sq.x: A GGAT letter dated 1 October 1982 warned of the archaeological sensitivity of Great House Farm. A copy was served on Cadw in September 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Cadw — Forensic Assessment v8.0.0 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E139 — 1 October 1982 GGAT warning about Great House Farm

sq.t: No document shows how Parcel A was acquired
sq.x: The registration narrative treats the conveyances as covering the farm as one holding. Western Ground Rents acquired Bute's fields (Parcel B) in 1938, but no document on file shows how it or BP acquired the farmhouse parcel (Parcel A).
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

sq.t: No historic conveyance supplies Parcel A's root
sq.x: The 1982–83 first registration merged both parcels into one estate, completed by the 1987 amalgamation. Parcel B had a paper root through Bute and WGR; for Parcel A the first-registration material identifies no historic conveyance supplying the root.

sq.t: 1982–83 title: no root for Parcel A
sq.x: Working theory: BP’s 1982–83 registration merged both parcels into a title with no documentary root for Parcel A, resting on failed attempts to make the occupation of Mary (Nancy) Williams look permissive.
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

sq.t: Absolute title may rest on unsupported extent
sq.x: Working theory: if HM Land Registry accepted absolute title to land whose extent the applicant’s deeds and prior title did not support, that would raise a question of registration mistake. The application plan, deeds, abstract and examination record would settle it.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Actual occupation overrides on registration
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams was in actual occupation when WA240304 was applied for in 1983. Under s.70(1)(g) Land Registration Act 1925 any proprietary right of hers bound BP on registration (compare Malory v Cheshire Homes [2002] EWCA Civ 151).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Death of Mary (Nancy) Williams, 1983
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, during the first-registration period. Her death and those of later witnesses removed first-hand knowledge of the parcel history.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Death of Mary (Nancy) Williams, 26 Mar 1983
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, while the first registration of the Great House Farm land to BP was in progress at HM Land Registry.
src: Legal Wiki: Potential Miscarriage of Justice: Issue Register

sq.t: Mary died in occupation, never a tenant
sq.x: Mary (Nancy) Williams died at the farmhouse on 26 March 1983 in occupation of the house parcel (Parcel A), never having signed a tenancy or accepted the licence; the date is also given in the European Commission's decision of 14 April 1989.

sq.t: William Buckler inherits and defends the case
sq.x: On Mary's death in 1983 her son William Buckler inherited her estate and defended the possession proceedings through 1992.
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Farm noted in conservation reports, 1983
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 26 October 1983 reported Great House Farm noted in conservation reports by the Community Council and Vale planners.

sq.t: Working theory: undisclosed evidence in 1984–87 litigation
sq.x: Working theory: if the 1984–87 litigation file shows BP held material evidence inconsistent with the case it put to the court and did not disclose it, in circumstances amounting to fraud, a Takhar ground to set aside the 1987 judgment arises.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Working theory: title never tried in 1984–87
sq.x: Working theory: in the 1984–87 litigation Mary's ownership case was set aside and the defence narrowed to adverse possession, leaving ownership of the house parcel untried (§2.1; A-076).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Two titles still live in 1986 litigation
sq.x: The 1986 litigation chronology shows two relevant titles still live, a point listed as an unresolved issue in the scrutiny of the combined process.
src: Legal Wiki: Potential Miscarriage of Justice: Issue Register

sq.t: Adverse-possession defence at High Court, 1986
sq.x: In the High Court action BP v Buckler (hearing 10 July 1986, judgment 24 July 1986), William (Billy) Buckler defended on adverse possession (EV-0074). The trial judgment is not yet held.

sq.t: House only partly recorded due to dispute
sq.x: RCAHMW recorded that the house was only partly recorded “because of problems created by an ownership dispute”, and that the Johns–Buckler correspondence has been lost “since 1986/87” (A-035, A-036).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Limitation clock treated farmhouse as tenancy land
sq.x: The Court of Appeal started the limitation clock in 1955 by treating the farmhouse as part of Frederick's tenancy. WGR's own May 1939 tenancy plan shows only the eastern fields (EV-0023). The judgment records the 1916 tenancy as of “the whole of the farm”.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

sq.t: Local Plan: buildings on site to be retained
sq.x: The East Vale Local Plan of February 1987 stated that the buildings on the Great House Farm site were to be retained.

sq.t: Title documents not produced in court
sq.x: The Court of Appeal dealt with limitation and licence and recorded that the title documents relied on were not produced. The documentary title and root of title to Parcel A have not been shown to have been fully examined in the surviving court record.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

sq.t: House of Lords leave-to-appeal petition, 1987
sq.x: After the 1987 Court of Appeal decision, leave to appeal was sought from the House of Lords. The petition papers, identified at The National Archives in September 2026, contradict the 1988 public statement that Mr Buckler “did not appeal”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E142 — 1987 House of Lords petition for leave to appeal: papers

sq.t: Appeal argued Mary held as owner, not licensee
sq.x: At the appeal hearing of 16–17 July 1987 it was argued that Mary never accepted the 1974 licence because she regarded herself as owner. The court held the 1962 action was in time and the 1974 letters made her possession permissive (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Court of Appeal leaves rectification open, 1987
sq.x: Dillon LJ stated that if Mary had acquired a valid title to the farmhouse and garden, it would have been an overriding interest binding BP’s registration, and her personal representatives would be entitled to seek rectification (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

sq.t: Appeal court finds joint adverse possession from 1955
sq.x: Dillon LJ described the trial judge’s treatment of Mary’s intention as paradoxical and found that Frederick and Mary were jointly in adverse possession of the farmhouse and garden from 2 February 1955. The appeal was dismissed because the 1962 order remained enforceable and the 1974 letters made Mary a licensee.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: 1987 judgment did not try title
sq.x: The 1987 judgment decided limitation and licence, not who owned Parcel A; it did not try title. Later decisions, including HM Land Registry’s 2026 complaint decisions, rely on it as if it settled title.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: Amalgamation does not prove root title
sq.x: A register amalgamation is an administrative title event. Its occurrence does not itself establish that the documentary root of title to Parcel A was correct.
src: Legal Wiki: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal

sq.t: Petition to the House of Lords, 1987–88
sq.x: Papers on a petition for leave to appeal to the House of Lords in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, 1987–88, are catalogued at the Parliamentary Archives (GHF-E142).
src: Legal Wiki: Parliamentary Archives — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E142 — 1987 House of Lords petition for leave to appeal: papers

sq.t: House of Lords refuses leave to appeal
sq.x: The House of Lords refused leave to appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler on 3 March 1988 (source pending: EV-0076).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

sq.t: Water supply cut off, 1988
sq.x: A cut-off of the water supply to the farm in 1988 is recorded (source pending); the date and the party responsible are not established.
src: Legal Wiki: Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: BP public statement, April 1988: “did not appeal”
sq.x: In April 1988 BP stated Mr Buckler had “lost the court hearing in Cardiff and did not appeal”; he had appealed to the Court of Appeal and sought House of Lords leave. Press reported Mary had “lost three previous High Court cases”; no court decided her ownership.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15 — South Wales Echo search-result extracts, April 1988 – March 1989 (index of 16 extracts)

sq.t: Rent-free stay framed as “ill health”
sq.x: A BP spokesman stated in April 1988 that Mary was allowed to live there rent-free “because of her ill health”. The 1974 letters followed directly on an undecided ownership plea and a revived possession order (N07, N15).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15 — South Wales Echo search-result extracts, April 1988 – March 1989 (index of 16 extracts)

sq.t: Echo prints “rent free” framing on eviction day
sq.x: On 29 April 1988, the day of the eviction attempt, the South Wales Echo printed that the dispute had “been waged for two generations”, that Mr Buckler’s mother had lost “three previous High Court cases”, and that “in 1974 BP Properties agreed to allow Mrs Buckler to remain in the farmhouse rent free”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-01 — Friday 29 April 1988: South Wales Echo (British Newspaper Archive extract)

sq.t: 29 April 1988 enforcement attempt fails
sq.x: On 29 April 1988 bailiffs and police attended Great House Farm to enforce possession; the drive was blocked and, after a stand-off involving a chainsaw, the attempt ended without the family being removed.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

sq.t: Bailiffs break in with poleaxes, Apr 1988
sq.x: South Wales Echo, c.30 Apr 1988, “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on”: “They smashed the lock on the gate and walked round the tractor … Then they started smashing the doors with poleaxes. My children were right behind the door when the axe came through.”
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

sq.t: Eviction attempt fails, 29 April 1988
sq.x: On 29 April 1988 an eviction attempt failed: the drive was blocked by a tractor, doors were axed, and William held the bailiffs off with a chainsaw; the bailiffs withdrew after four hours.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: First bailiff eviction attempt, 29 Apr 1988
sq.x: A press report recorded five bailiffs and around 15 police officers at the first eviction attempt on 29 April 1988, with South Wales Police stating officers were there to prevent a breach of the peace. The South Wales Echo of 30 April reported a dozen police on the farm.
src: Legal Wiki: South Wales Police — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

sq.t: First eviction attempt: a dozen police present
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 30 April 1988 reported that “a dozen police officers were on the farm as the bailiffs tried to evict the Buckler family”, and that Mr Buckler refused to leave Great House Farm for a medical check-up because he feared the bailiffs would return.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-02 — Saturday 30 April 1988: South Wales Echo (British Newspaper Archive extract)

sq.t: Four-hour stand-off with bailiffs, 29 Apr 1988
sq.x: Five bailiffs and about 15 police arrived. William Buckler blocked the drive with a tractor and barred the doors; bailiffs broke the doors with poleaxes and withdrew after a four-hour stand-off. William told the press: “They have got no documents for it. If it’s theirs, why have I never paid a penny in rent for it in my life?” (N07)

sq.t: Press: “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on”
sq.x: A newspaper report headed “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” was published around 30 April 1988, during the dispute over the trees and the possession order at Tŷ Mawr (Great House Farm).
src: Legal Wiki: Home Office — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

sq.t: Press: Mary “fought and lost” three cases
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 29 April 1988 reported that Mary had “fought and lost three previous High Court cases” over ownership. The court record shows no case in which her ownership was decided; the 1955 action was against Frederick alone.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

sq.t: “BP signal Welsh sales”, July 1988
sq.x: On 9 July 1988, between the April stand-off and the November eviction, the Estates Gazette reported “BP signal Welsh sales”, naming Ropemaker Properties with Debenham Tewson as agents (EV-0093).

sq.t: Farm and barn rejected for listing, 1988
sq.x: Cadw’s 1988 listed-buildings survey assessed Great House Farm and its barn and rejected both for listing. Two photographs dated 29 July 1988 survive, coded “YYY”, meaning “marginally below the bar”.

sq.t: Great House rejected in 1988 listing survey
sq.x: Cadw wrote in May 2026 that Great House Farm and the barn were “assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough”, graded marginally below the bar on 29 July 1988. The list that survey produced was issued on 6 April 1989, listing three Llandough buildings.

sq.t: No Cadw record from July to December 1988
sq.x: No Cadw record has been produced for the five months between its 29 July 1988 photographs of the house and the early-December 1988 listing consideration.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Farmhouse and barn rejected for listing, 1988
sq.x: Cadw’s listed-buildings casework stated on 21 May 2026 that the farmhouse and barn were assessed and rejected in the 1988 Llandough community survey, and supplied no other electronic records of the decision.
src: Legal Wiki: Cadw — Forensic Assessment v8.0.0 (full text)
Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

sq.t: Five-month gap after July 1988 inspection
sq.x: Five months passed after Cadw's 29 July 1988 inspection; what triggered the December 1988 assessment is unknown.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Cadw letter to Minister on spot-listing not located
sq.x: A 1988 Cadw letter to a Minister concerning spot-listing of the farmhouse is reserved as GHF-E152; the original has not been located.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E152 — Cadw letter to the Minister concerning spot-listing, 1988 (awaited original)

sq.t: BP Pension Fund sells Llandough and Leckwith woods
sq.x: South Wales Echo reports of 1989–90 recorded that woodland was “sold to the LAW by BP Pension Fund which owned it until 1988”, including seven woods “in Llandough and Leckwith”, among them Coed Cwm Cydfin, and that the Land Authority for Wales advertised Llandough “Prime Residential Building Land”.

sq.t: House of Lords leave to appeal refused
sq.x: Western Mail, 6 Dec 1988, reported that the Bucklers had unsuccessfully sought leave to appeal to the House of Lords, an Appeal Committee ruling they had exhausted the remedies available under the laws of England and Wales.
src: Legal Wiki: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing”

sq.t: BP Pension Fund sells 1,300 Welsh acres
sq.x: In October–November 1988 the BP Pension Fund sold about 1,300 acres of Welsh land to Intercontinental Land & Development (Cardiff) Ltd for £29,375,400; the farm site stayed with BP Properties Ltd (EV-0270).

sq.t: Surviving ITV clip is a later copy
sq.x: The viewing copy of the HTV report (GHF-E113) carries an “itv CYMRU WALES” identifier, a brand first used in 2014. The original transmission, its duration and its edit history have not been established.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

sq.t: A witness’s recollection of the 1988 removal
sq.x: [name withheld] recalled in September 2026 that she went to the farm during the 1988 removal to fetch medicine from the house, not to serve the writ as ITV presented it. She stated that men who appeared to be soldiers dragged her, kicked her and threw her over the gate; ITV footage shows her arm in a sling.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E114 — witness recollection: September 2026 recollection of the 1988 removal

sq.t: Abrupt cut after “prime development land” line
sq.x: The surviving clip cuts abruptly after the voice-over describes the land as “prime development land overlooking Cardiff” and shows a figure in paramilitary-style dress. Whether this was the original edit or a later re-edit is not established; no censorship finding is made.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Bailiffs remove the family; house later demolished
sq.x: In late November 1988 BP’s enforcement agents and bailiffs entered Great House Farm and removed the occupying family. Injunction proceedings followed, and the farmhouse was demolished in early December 1988.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation

sq.t: Broadcast clip omits pregnancy and infant children
sq.x: The surviving clip of the 1988 report does not mention that the mother was pregnant or that three infant children lived at the farm. Whether the original broadcast included this has not been established.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: Forced entry and roof stripped, 30 Nov 1988
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 30 November 1988 reported that those who “forced their way into the 400-year-old Great House Farm” already had “half the roof off one of the outbuildings”, and that [name withheld] feared BP Properties would now flatten the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-04 — South Wales Echo search extract, Wednesday 30 November 1988

sq.t: ITV Wales films eviction aftermath, 1988
sq.x: An ITV Cymru Wales report recorded the aftermath of the 1988 possession enforcement at Great House Farm, the injunction, BP’s position, a reference to the site as development land, and [name withheld] with her arm in a sling.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

sq.t: Police removal of documents, 1988, no inventory
sq.x: Documents were removed during a police search in 1988; no inventory has been traced (A-034, source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”
sq.x: The South Wales Echo front page of about 30 November 1988 (Peter Bibby) carried the headlines “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”, “A bitter feud over rights that lasted 33 years” and “Action on farm”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N14 — “Angry scenes as farmer evicted” (South Wales Echo front page, c. 30 November 1988)

sq.t: Mary’s papers and journal lost in eviction
sq.x: Possessions including Mary’s papers, photographs and journal were left in the house or thrown into the road during the November 1988 eviction (source pending). William Buckler put the loss at about £30,000 (South Wales Echo, 1989; N13).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: Possession taken; bailiffs force entry, Nov 1988
sq.x: On 29/30 November 1988 possession was obtained; bailiffs forced entry and William was taken to Llandough Hospital (press, Wednesday 30 November).
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

sq.t: Bailiffs evict the Bucklers, 30 Nov 1988
sq.x: On 30 November 1988 the South Wales Echo front page ran “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”. Bailiffs who forced entry had already removed half the roof of one outbuilding, and [name withheld] feared BP would flatten the farmhouse (N14, N15).

sq.t: HTV “Eviction News Material”, 30 Nov 1988
sq.x: National Library of Wales catalogue item 507738, “Eviction News Material, 30 November 1988”, records a one-minute HTV Wales item: bailiffs removing furniture, removal vans, and [name withheld] leaving the farm, with a report that the High Court granted an injunction stopping BP demolishing the farm.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”, 1988
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of about 30 Nov 1988 reported the eviction under the headline “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N14 — “Angry scenes as farmer evicted” (South Wales Echo front page, c. 30 November 1988)

sq.t: Eviction tape catalogued “Not viewed”
sq.x: The National Library of Wales record for the 30 November 1988 eviction tape reads “Not viewed”; the clip's position on the tape is unknown and no catalogue or online-publication date appears. The separate 5 December 1988 “Wales at Six” demolition report has not been located.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

sq.t: HTV Wales films the eviction, 30 Nov 1988
sq.x: National Library of Wales catalogue item 507738, “Eviction News Material, 30 November 1988”, is a one-minute HTV Wales videocassette recorded and broadcast on 30 Nov 1988.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

sq.t: Only five seconds of ITV eviction coverage found
sq.x: A five-second clip of Great House Farm survives from ITV coverage broadcast between sports programmes. The remainder of the broadcast has not been located; ITV archive, transmission records and production files would show what the unseen material contained.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: ITV clip omits pregnancy and children
sq.x: A separate ITV clip of the 1988 events contains abrupt transitions and apparent omissions; it does not mention that [name withheld] was pregnant or that children were in the house.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

sq.t: Farmer taken from hospital bed to face charges
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 3 December 1988 reported that evicted farmer Bill Buckler, 40, “caught up in a 33-year wrangle”, was taken from his hospital bed to face charges of assaulting two bailiffs.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-06 — South Wales Echo search extract, Saturday 3 December 1988

sq.t: HTV report: “SAS style” eviction, “prime development land”
sq.x: An HTV Wales report (GHF-E113), reporter Miles Fletcher, presenter Nicola Heywood-Thomas, described the eviction as “SAS style”, called the site “prime development land overlooking Cardiff”, and reported a High Court injunction stopping BP demolishing the farm. Transmission date not yet identified.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

sq.t: High Court summons against BP, Dec 1988
sq.x: The South Wales Echo of 2 December 1988 reported that a summons against BP would be heard on Monday 5 December; Mr Justice Anthony Evans allowed that the family could enter the house to collect belongings only “as long as BP solicitors agree”. The family had also lodged a petition.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-05 — South Wales Echo search extract, Friday 2 December 1988

sq.t: Occupiers not consulted on listing
sq.x: The occupiers were not consulted on listing of the farmhouse; the Cadw report accepts this was not then a statutory duty (Cadw report VI.5).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Programme calls the removal “SAS-style operation”
sq.x: A contemporary television programme described the manner of the 1988 removal as an “SAS-style operation”. The wording does not establish that the personnel were SAS.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation

sq.t: “Regaining possession”: wording that assumes entitlement
sq.x: BP and press wording described the 1988 events as “regaining possession”, language that assumes a prior legal entitlement to possession rather than describing the event.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation

sq.t: Cadw publicly “considering” listing after July coding
sq.x: Cadw publicly stated in December 1988 that it was “considering” listing, after coding the farmhouse below the bar in July 1988 (Cadw report VI.3).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: No sign earlier surveys were considered
sq.x: Cadw could not confirm whether the 1974 RCAHMW survey, the Sites and Monuments Record, GGAT's 1978–80 work or the 1982 warning were considered in its 1988 assessment (Cadw report VII.2–3).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Res judicata and abuse of process bar
sq.x: A judgment binds the parties and their successors in title, including Mary's estate; points that could have been raised may be barred (Henderson v Henderson; Johnson v Gore Wood [2002] 2 AC 1), save for special circumstances such as new material (Arnold v NatWest [1991] 2 AC 93).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Fraud requires proof of conscious dishonesty
sq.x: Deceit, or setting aside a judgment for fraud, requires proof of conscious dishonesty judged by the standards of honest people (Ivey v Genting Casinos [2017] UKSC 67). Negligence, muddle, lost files and changing explanations are not fraud.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Limitation largely expired; s.32 needs concealment
sq.x: Most limitation periods expired long ago; s.32 Limitation Act 1980 needs proof of deliberate concealment, not just loss. Time runs from discovery, and many key records surfaced only in 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: LRA 1925 ss.115–116: suppression in registration
sq.x: The Land Registration Act 1925 contained express provisions on suppression of documents or facts in registration proceedings (s.115) and fraudulent procurement of register entries (s.116), the historical legal test for the 1982–84 registrations.

sq.t: Land Registration Act 1925 s.115: concealment offence
sq.x: Section 115 of the Land Registration Act 1925 made fraudulent concealment of a document or fact material to title in registration proceedings an offence. Working theory: the 1982–83 applications may engage it, a legal test to apply once the file is read.

sq.t: Occupier’s rights bind every later buyer
sq.x: Under the doctrine of notice (Hunt v Luck, 1902) anyone acquiring land was fixed with notice of the rights of the person in actual occupation. From 1926, Land Registration Act 1925 s.70(1)(g) made those rights overriding interests.

sq.t: Taking title deeds was a felony in 1950
sq.x: Taking documents of title to land was a felony under the Larceny Act 1916 (s.7), and knowingly receiving them a separate offence. The Limitation Act 1939 (s.26) already postponed limitation where a right of action was concealed by fraud.

sq.t: Green registration did not vest ownership
sq.x: Under the Commons Registration Act 1965 as enacted, registration of a village green did not by itself vest the land in a local authority; registration is not a conveyance of ownership.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

sq.t: Limitation Act s.32: concealment postpones time
sq.x: Section 32 of the Limitation Act 1980 postpones time where an action is based on fraud or a relevant fact was deliberately concealed; concealment needs no pre-existing duty to disclose (Canada Square v Potter [2023] UKSC 41). Section 32(3) protects a later innocent purchaser for value.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

sq.t: Stolen chattels are not time-barred
sq.x: Limitation Act 1980 s.4: no limitation period runs for a stolen chattel, except against a later good-faith purchaser. Working theory: if the 1950–52 family papers or the 1988 house contents were stolen, ownership of them survives.

sq.t: 1997 Act removes six-year indemnity bar
sq.x: Section 83(11) of the Land Registration Act 1925 set a special six-year period from registration for some indemnity applications. Section 2 of the Land Registration Act 1997 substituted a new section 83 without that registration-date limit.

sq.t: CPR 52.30: reopening a final appeal
sq.x: CPR 52.30 allows a final appeal determination to be reopened where necessary to avoid real injustice, the circumstances are exceptional and there is no alternative effective remedy; permission is required.

sq.t: LRA 2002: register alteration and rectification
sq.x: The Land Registration Act 2002 provides alteration and rectification routes (Schedule 4) and an indemnity regime (Schedule 8). For the woodland, the remedy can be rectification if an identified polygon is family land, subject to protections for the later registered proprietor.

sq.t: Takhar: fraudulent judgment can be set aside
sq.x: Takhar v Gracefield Developments Ltd [2019] UKSC 13 holds that a judgment obtained by fraud may be set aside by a fresh action without showing the fraud could not have been discovered earlier; the fraud must be material, an operative cause of the decision (RBS v Highland [2013] EWCA Civ 328).

sq.t: Registry indemnity time runs from knowledge
sq.x: Under Land Registration Act 2002 Schedule 8 paragraph 8, time for an indemnity application runs from when the applicant knew, or might have known, of the grounds. The April 1983 registration correspondence was first identified in July 2026.
